verified.description: The recursive delete expands an unquoted, unvalidated $dir. An empty or missing argument turns it into rm -rf /tmp/*, and a path with spaces splits into several targets. Before the cd on line 5 was checked, a failed cd also sent the find on line 6 into the wrong tree; line 7 does not depend on the cd at all.
verified.recommendation: Require a non-empty existing directory argument and quote the expansion: rm -rf -- "${dir:?}"/tmp/*.
